name: Portland Environmental Services news RSS (CSO Advisories and Sewage Advisories)
operator: City of Portland Bureau of Environmental Services
waters_covered: Willamette River (downstream of Ross Island Bridge), Columbia Slough, Portland creeks (e.g. Woods Creek, Tryon Creek)
access_detail: RSS 2.0, no auth (raw/bes-news-rss-items.json, titles/links/dates only). Items titled 'CSO Advisory: ...' or 'Sewage Advisory: ...' / 'Advisory: Sewage Release to ...'. Each article page states 'Published <date time>', 'Updated <date time>', 'This advisory expired at <time> on <date>', the affected stretch, 'The overflow started around 4:20 pm on December 18', and the advice 'Avoid contact with the river in the affected area during the overflow and for 48 hours after it stops'. Recent items: 2026-10-22 sewage release to Woods Creek; 2026-10-06 sewage release SW Portland; 2026-07-08 Elk Rock Pump Station release to the Willamette.
cadence: Issued during the event (CSO advisory the same day; 2025-12-18 published 4:45 pm for an overflow that began 4:20 pm). Expiry 48 hours after the overflow ends.
history: Articles back to at least 2021 on portland.gov/bes/news; the RSS holds the latest items only.
legal_basis: NPDES OR0026905 CSO public notification; permit Schedule F public notification of overflow
status_reason: Read every refresh by the Oregon ingester (rules only): each CSO Advisory and Sewage Advisory is a dated sewage report with the start, end and stretch its text gives; the City's 48-hour window after the overflow stops is the authority's own red. 13 advisories (4 CSO) in the 25 items read 2026-11-07.
notes: Mix of CSO and SSO advisories with other news; filter by title.

name: Portland Big Pipe Tracker (gauge and 72-hour chart)
operator: City of Portland Bureau of Environmental Services
access_detail: The tracker page (https://www.portland.gov/bes/big-pipe-tracker) says 'Current CSO Advisories: There is no current CSO advisory in effect.' (2026-11-07); the gauge (https://www.portlandoregon.gov/bes/bigpipe/gauge.cfm) answered 'BES Big Pipe Gauge 0 % Nov 7, 2026 3:45 pm'. 'Data are updated every 15 minutes, with up to a 45-minute lag time.' A 72-hour chart (chart.cfm). Email list: GovDelivery ORPORTLAND_ENT signup 39493.
status_reason: Registered as a monitored page: the tracker's current-advisory sentence and the gauge's fill level. A fill level is not a report of an overflow, so it colours nothing; the advisories themselves are read from the news feed.

name: Portland Combined Sewer Overflow Advisories email list (GovDelivery)
operator: City of Portland Bureau of Environmental Services

name: Oregon DEQ: All spills reported to OERS and verified by DEQ, 2013-08-01 to 2025-03-27 (ArcGIS FeatureServer)
access_detail: Hosted feature layer (org uUvqNMGPm7axC2dD, the Oregon state ArcGIS Online org), hasStaticData true. 13,337 spills; 2,371 with Material 'Sewage' (MaterialCategory 'Sewage, Stormwater, Wastewater, Floodwater, & Biological' 2,844). Query works with where/outStatistics; export csv/geojson allowed. Sample raw/oers-spills-sewage-sample.json (Situation narratives dropped: they carry personal names).

sample_record.Name: Sewage - [house number removed] N Main Ave (the Name field is never read by the ingester)

cadence: Static snapshot; last row 2025-03-27. No live successor found.
legal_basis: OAR 340-142 (spill reporting to OERS); permit Schedule F
status_reason: Read once as a frozen archive by the Oregon ingester: the 2,371 sewage rows (2013-07-24 to 2025-03-27) with DEQ's point, the report date and time, gallons and the affected water where given; the narrative, title and address are never read. The layer is checked each run for an edit.
notes: Situation narratives contain names of callers and contractors: never ingest.

name: Oregon DEQ Sanitary Sewer Overflow Report Form (5-day written report)
status_reason: Shows the regulator report: OERS by phone within 24 hours, written within 5 days, with a public notification section.

name: DEQ NPDES/WPCF General Conditions (Schedule F): public notification of effluent violation or overflow
status_reason: Oregon's public duty is a permit condition, not a statute.
notes: Quoted (WPCF domestic general conditions, 2009; NPDES Schedule F carries the same text, search_only): 'If effluent limitations specified in this permit are exceeded or an overflow occurs that threatens public health, the permittee must take such steps as are necessary to alert the public, health agencies and other affected entities (e.g., public water systems) about the extent and nature of the discharge in accordance with the notification procedures specified in this permit or as specified in its Emergency Response and Public Notification Plan'. Schedule F D.5: oral report within 24 hours (OERS 1-800-452-0311), written within 5 days.

name: OAR 340-142-0040 Required reporting (spills to OERS)
status_reason: Immediate phone report to OERS for reportable releases; sewage is reported through permits.

name: Oregon Beach Monitoring Program advisories (OHA with DEQ)
waters_covered: Oregon coast, 360 miles, May to September
access_detail: 'Check Current Beach Conditions' (https://www.oregon.gov/oha/PH/HEALTHYENVIRONMENTS/RECREATION/BEACHWATERQUALITY/Pages/status.aspx): an HTML table per coast (County, Beach, Status) with the statuses OPEN, ADVISORY, SEWAGE ('Sewage spills or major pollution events occurred. Avoid swimming or water contact.') and NO MONITORING; 'The 2026 monitoring season has ended' on 2026-11-07 (every beach NO MONITORING). GovDelivery topic ORHA_190 for advisory notices; a Beach Partner List by email request.
status_reason: Read every refresh as a snapshot by the Oregon ingester: ADVISORY as OHA's beach advisory, SEWAGE as OHA's sewage advisory; OPEN and NO MONITORING are no record. Out of season on 2026-11-07 (33 beaches, all NO MONITORING): the reader is tested on a fixture in the page's markup; check its first reads in May 2027.

name: OHA cyanoHAB recreational use advisories (ArcGIS FeatureServer)
access_detail: 64 features; fields WaterbodyName, AdvisoryStatus (Advisory, Precaution, ...), Toxin, ToxinLevel, Details, AdvisoryLink, Issue_Date, County_1/2, EditDate. Polygon layer HABs_Advisories_(Polygon2); archive OR_HABs_Advisory_Archive. Public page https://www.oregon.gov/oha/ph/healthyenvironments/recreation/harmfulalgaeblooms/pages/blue-greenalgaeadvisories.aspx. Sample raw/oha-hab-points-sample.json (Creator/Editor usernames removed).
cadence: 'updated regularly ... as advisories are issued and lifted'
status_reason: Read every refresh through the generic ArcGIS block: OHA's advisories and precautions (39 of 64 rows on 2026-11-07: 5 Advisory, 34 Precaution) as algal-bloom advisories; 'Below Human RUV' and 'Advisory/Precaution Lifted' are no current advisory.
notes: Includes a 'PERMANENT RECREATIONAL USE ADVISORY' for the South Umpqua.

name: Oak Lodge Water Services overflow posts
status_reason: A small district that posts each overflow as a news article (2025-12-18: three lift stations, impacts to Kellogg Creek and the Willamette River, the advice to avoid contact for 48 hours afterwards). Registered as a monitored page; HTML only, no feed.

name: City of Astoria Wastewater / CSO page
status_reason: Background only; 38 open CSO outfalls to the Columbia River and Youngs Bay; no event notices on the page (answered 200 on 2026-11-07). Registered with the barrier: no web channel.

name: City of Corvallis Public Notification & Spill Response Plan
status_reason: The plan page answered 200 on 2026-11-07 (navigation only extracted); signs and media contacts for larger discharges; no event list. Registered with the barrier: no web channel.

status_reason: Commercial bay closures follow sewage events (e.g. Tillamook); a 2017 ArcGIS closure layer exists in the state org. Not fetched.
